page: Amazon Web Services c7i.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by a custom Intel Xeon Platinum 8488C processor running at a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The instance provisions 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU includes 105 MB of L3 cache alongside hardware-level acceleration features such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 vector instruction sets. Memory resources total 32.0 GB of DDR5 operating at 5000 MHz, providing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Benchmark assessments demonstrate consistent mid-tier compute throughput across synthetic and application-level workloads. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1741.0 and a multi-core score of 10360.0, backed by a PassMark CPU score of 22580.69. Memory tests indicate uncached large-block read speeds of 83.57 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 57.73 GB/sec, though the overall PassMark memory score falls into the lower quartile. The hardware supports INT8 matrix acceleration via AMX, yielding text generation throughput of 11.18 tokens per second on 7-billion parameter language models without dedicated accelerator hardware.

The server includes 6 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and operates without attached local instance storage or bundled complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Persistent disk functionality requires remote storage volume attachments. Given its 1:2 memory-to-vCPU distribution and compute-dense silicon profile, the c7i.4xlarge offers a balanced resource profile for compute-bound tasks like software builds, web serving fleets, media transcoding, and moderate data batch processing.
description: Amazon Web Services c7i.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8488C processor operating at 3.2 GHz. Supported by the Nitro hypervisor, the instance includes 8 physical cores with multi-threading, 105 MB of L3 cache, and instruction support for AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Memory capacity is 32.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM, delivering a 1:2 memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Networking operates with a 6 Gbps baseline, with no integrated local storage or GPU accelerators present. Standard benchmarks place its processing capabilities squarely in the middle tier, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 22580.69 and multi-core Geekbench performance of 10360.0. The c7i.4xlarge is designed for compute-centric workloads, including continuous integration pipelines, batch transformation jobs, Redis caching layers, and web application serving.
